title: GPT-6.2 Astra on iac-bench 2026-11

## Summary


GPT-6.2 Astra is new in 2026-11. It ranks sixth of 24 with an overall composite of 87.3 and a 95% rank interval of 6–7. It finishes ahead of GPT-6.1 Terra, the model just below it, in 82% of bootstrap resamples, so the two are within the margin of three samples. It is clearly separated from the models on either side of that pair: it essentially never finishes ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol or the four models above it, and essentially always ahead of Claude Haiku 5.5.


All 18 attempts planned, with no security findings and no known apply failure. Its best placings are the Aurora global database (G004, 88.1, fifth, with the third-highest rubric median) and App Service (G003, 93.7, sixth). S3 (G001, 78.0, 19th) and Cloud SQL (G002, 84.8, 18th) are its weakest. Its worst attempt scores 77.0, the fourth-highest worst case in the field.


The judge rates its short, opinionated modules more highly than the rubric does. Its judge-only score (95.2) ranks third and its mechanical-only score (84.1) seventh, the second-largest gap in the field after Claude Sonnet 5.5. Its judge medians run from 86.8 to 100 on every fixture; the rubric charges it for the inputs and operational features those modules leave out.


It is also the fastest and shortest writer in the field: a median of 98 seconds and 2,917 output tokens per attempt. All 18 attempts cost $4.48.


## Changes since the 2026-10 report


GPT-6.2 Astra was not part of the 2026-10 release; this is its first report.

## Strengths


- **Very small interfaces.** Median inputs are 2 on S3 and on the storage account (G006), 7 on GKE (G005), 11 on G004, 12 on App Service (G003) and 14 on Cloud SQL (G002). Every storage-account attempt asks only for the resource group and the application's principal, and derives the account name and location itself (E4, E7, 3/3).
- **Security fixed in code in all 18 attempts.** On S3 it enforces bucket-owner ownership and a TLS-deny policy (E1, E4, 3/3); on the storage account, shared keys and nested public access are off and the portal defaults to Entra ID (E2, 3/3).
- **App Service near the top of the rubric.** Rubric median 0.977, tied fourth in the field, with managed-identity image pulls and a metric alert in 3/3 (E3, E4). Its only rubric loss on App Service is missing output descriptions (G003` B2` ).
- **An Aurora global database that deploys (3/3).** Each region's cluster is declared in a local child module (` regional/` ) that the root calls once per region (excerpt below). The module creates a KMS key in its own region, sets` storage_encrypted = true` , and attaches a parameter group with` rds.force_ssl = "1"` , so neither known apply failure occurs. No attempt sets` manage_master_user_password` . Two generate the master password with` random_password` and keep a copy in a Secrets Manager secret (G004` H9` at 0.5, since the password lands in state); G004 e1 passes an ephemeral input to the write-only` master_password_wo` , which G004` H9` scores as a raw input. Rubric median 0.890, third in the field; judge median 92.1, tied second.
- **Judged clean on the doctrine's structural sections.** *Internal logic* , *Scope* , *Inline Resource Configuration* , *Sensitive values* , *Lifecycle meta-arguments* and the anti-pattern sections are 2 in all 54 readings.


## Weaknesses


- **G004 settings with no inputs (3/3).** Deletion protection and the final snapshot are hardcoded (G004` H11` /` H12` at 0.75), and instance count (two per region) and backup retention (35 days) have no inputs (G004` A7` ,` A8` ). No attempt loads pgaudit, logs connections or enables enhanced monitoring (E1, E2, E4, 0/3).
- **Minimal S3 buckets.** The only lifecycle rule aborts incomplete multipart uploads, so transition, expiration and noncurrent-version rules are missing (G001` H6` ,` H7` , 3/3), and no attempt offers access logging (G001` H9` ,` H13` ), a region input (G001` H15` ) or a way to set` force_destroy` (G001` H14` ), all 3/3. GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6.1 Terra lose the same lifecycle and logging items.
- **Cloud SQL gaps (3/3).** No` deletion_policy` on databases (G002` H11` ), backups and point-in-time recovery always on (G002` H4` /` H5` at 0.75), no labels input (G002` H8` ), the region fed to the instance rather than the provider (G002` H9` at 0.5), and no` cloudsql.instanceUser` grant for the IAM users it creates (E6, 0/3).
- **Storage account inputs too few to cover the application.** No attempt takes the application's containers (G006` A6` ) or tags (G006` A5` ), two cannot influence the account name (G006` A1` ), two hardcode` LRS` (G006` H8` ), and none offers blob access logs (G006` H7` ).
- **GKE without CMEK, labels or connection outputs.** No attempt accepts a Cloud KMS key for Secrets (G005` H9` ) or a labels input (G005` A4` ), two set no maintenance window (G005` H7` ), and the judge noted in every attempt that the outputs omit the cluster endpoint and CA certificate.
- **Provider constraints that admit a new major** in 12 of 18 attempts (` B1` ):` >= 5.0, < 7.0` on S3,` >= 6.0, < 8.0` on Cloud SQL and GKE. On G004 the child module declares` hashicorp/aws` with no version constraint in all three attempts.
- **Missing descriptions** on Cloud SQL (2/3), App Service (3/3), G004 (3/3) and GKE (1/3) (` B2` ). The judge gave *Documentation* 1 in every App Service and G004 reading.


## Characteristic patterns


- **Single-file modules.** G001 e3 and G006 e3 put the terraform block, variables, resources and outputs in one` main.tf` ( *File layout* 0); several others keep outputs in` main.tf` . *File layout* is its lowest judged section (27 of 54 readings at 2).
- **Hardcoded decisions instead of inputs,** such as LRS or ZRS redundancy, two instances per region and 35-day backups on G004, and always-on Cloud SQL backups. The judge reads these as settled decisions ( *Interface design* 2 in 53 of 54 readings); the rubric charges for the exposure and opt-out items they remove.
- **Registry identity passed twice on App Service.** Every attempt takes an ACR resource ID beside a registry URL or a client ID that could be looked up ( *Data sources vs inputs* 1 in all nine readings), and the image regex rejects digest references in two attempts.


## Representative excerpt


` G004/gpt-6.2-astra-e1/regional/main.tf` lines 84–99


```text
resource "aws_rds_cluster" "db" {
cluster_identifier                  = var.name
engine                              = "aurora-postgresql"
engine_version                      = var.engine_version
global_cluster_identifier           = var.global_id
source_region                       = var.source_region
database_name                       = var.source_region == null ? var.database : null
master_username                     = var.source_region == null ? "clusteradmin" : null
master_password_wo                  = var.password
master_password_wo_version          = var.password_version
port                                = 5432
db_subnet_group_name                = aws_db_subnet_group.db.name
vpc_security_group_ids              = [aws_security_group.db.id]
db_cluster_parameter_group_name     = aws_rds_cluster_parameter_group.pg.name
storage_encrypted                   = true
kms_key_id                          = aws_kms_key.db.arn


```


Each region's Aurora cluster is declared in a local child module, called once per region from the root. The cluster takes a write-only master password, encrypts its storage with a KMS key created in the same region and names a parameter group that sets rds.force_ssl. All three G004 attempts use this structure.
